input.body:
Dear Student Finance Office,

I am writing as Kinwarden, on behalf of the family of Ms [PERSON_2], who has been told she holds an offer for the MSc Finance programme starting January 2027.

We have been given a document by an education consultant, Mr. Mark Benson of Global Pathways Education, said to be issued by your Office of International Admissions under reference KGU/INT/2026/77812 and dated 21 October 2026. It states an unconditional offer with a 40% International Excellence Scholarship, first-year tuition of GBP 18,500 after the scholarship, and a "visa guarantee fee" of GBP 1,200, both payable to Global Pathways Education (Pvt) Ltd at Indus Crescent Bank, Karachi.

Before any money is sent, please could you confirm the following in one reply:

1. Does Ms [PERSON_2] hold a current offer for the MSc Finance programme starting January 2027, and does reference KGU/INT/2026/77812 correspond to a genuine offer in your records?
2. Is Global Pathways Education (Pvt) Ltd, or Mr. Mark Benson, an authorised representative or agent of Kingsgate University London for the receipt of tuition or other fees?
3. What is the correct amount payable to secure her place, and the official deadline for payment?
4. Please confirm that all fees are payable only to the university's own account, and send your bank details (account name, account number/IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, bank name) on official university letterhead, together with any deposit or fee statement.
5. What is her Student ID, for use as the payment reference, and is there any other reference your bank requires?
6. Does the university charge any visa or "visa guarantee" fee separately from tuition?

We are also contacting you at this address only, as it is your verified contact, and not at the free email address quoted in the document we were given.

Thank you for your help — the family is anxious to settle whatever is genuinely owed.

Kind regards,
Kinwarden, on behalf of the family of [PERSON_2]
Ref: KGU/INT/2026/77812

I've read the letter, flagged it, and written to the university. Here's where things stand.

**What I found in the offer letter — strong signs of a scam:**
- Tuition is to be paid to **Global Pathways Education (Pvt) Ltd**, the consultant's own company in Karachi — not to Kingsgate University.
- A **GBP 1,200 "visa guarantee fee"** — universities don't charge such a fee.
- Replies go to a **personal Gmail address** and a WhatsApp mobile, not the university's official domain.
- A **Friday deadline** ("seat goes to someone else") and **PKR 350,000 already taken in cash** as a "processing fee" — money paid to a person, in cash, for a "guarantee".

**What I've done:**
- Flagged the letter as a security event in the case.
- Emailed Kingsgate University's verified finance office asking, in one message, whether [PERSON_2] actually holds an offer under ref KGU/INT/2026/77812, whether Mr. Benson or his company is an authorised representative, the correct amount and deadline, and their official bank details on letterhead.
- Warned the family plainly and asked them to stop sending Mr. Benson money.

**What happens next:** I will not propose any payment, prepare any forms, or price a transfer until the university confirms the admission directly. A reminder is set for 48 hours to chase them if they haven't answered. If the offer proves genuine, I'll verify the university's own account and pay only that. If the university has no such applicant, I'll tell the family gently, make clear it is not their fault, and advise them to keep all letters and receipts and report it to the police.

I have an answer from Kingsgate University London's finance office, writing from their official address, and I'm sorry to say it is not the news we hoped for.

They have no applicant or student named [PERSON_2] in their admissions records, and no offer has ever been issued in her name. They confirm they never charge a "visa guarantee" fee, and that no agent or consultant ever collects tuition for them. The offer letter Mr. Benson sent is not from the university.

Please be clear on this: it is not your fault. These scams are built to look exactly like a real offer, and parents all over the world are caught by them. Nothing has been paid through Kinwarden, and no invoice was ever raised.

What to do now:
• Do not send Mr. Benson or Global Pathways any more money, and stop contact with him.
• Keep the offer letter, all messages, his bank details and any receipts for the PKR 350,000 — they are evidence.
• Report it to your local police (in Pakistan you can also report it to the FIA cybercrime wing), and mention you have the consultant's bank account details.
• Please also tell your daughter's school or any other families who may be talking to this agent.

The university has alerted its own fraud team. There are no bills for us to pay here, so I am closing the case — but write to me any time if you need help with a police report or a genuine university application.
